correctness.rationale: The count is indexed by increasing start positions i<j, so each candidate is counted once. Substituting j'=j−(m+g−1) gives 1≤i<j'≤n−2m−g+2 and hence the stated binomial count, also zero when no pair fits. Each event imposes a matching of m complement constraints, so has probability q^(−m). At different endpoint sums c and c' the matchings have no common edge. A cycle would have to alternate colors; every two successive reflection steps would advance by the same nonzero translation c'−c (with a fixed choice of first color), which cannot close. Each edge of the resulting forest costs one factor q^(−1), by rooting each component, proving pairwise independence even with intersecting supports. At one endpoint sum the starts are (i,j) and (i+d,j−d); all constraints belong to one matching. The left intervals overlap in max(m−d,0) sites, which is exactly their number of shared edges, since all left endpoints lie strictly below the common geometric center. There are B(n−2m−g−2d+2) unordered pairs of this type at shift d, from the stricter inner-stem separation. Summation of the diagonal and twice these unordered-pair covariances gives the displayed variance including empty and m=1 cases. For fixed m,g each shifted binomial count is asymptotic to the first; the geometric sum then yields the successive limit (q+1)/(q−1). Substitution for q=4,m=2,g=0 gives (15B(n−2)+6B(n−4))/256 and ratio 21/16.
residual_risks: Distinct-center independence is pairwise, not mutual. The model counts candidate complementary factors in a uniform abstract word, not selected folds; the limiting variance ratio takes n to infinity first.

evidence: Burden et al. define D2 match indicators between two random sequences and analyze overlap covariance; Remark 4.7 identifies zero covariance for certain uniform-law overlaps. Their introduction credits earlier expectation and variance bounds. Fitch's bibliographic title suggests a closely related expectation calculation, but no decisive passage was accessible.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The two-sequence dependence analysis is relevant but does not directly model one word in which a position can be used on opposite stem sides by different candidates. The one-word reflection-center proof covers that case and counts the near-diagonal same-center dependence. The actual scope of Fitch remains unresolved.

evidence: Known avoidance covers no-occurrence words, and the inspected match-count source provides a different overlap stratification. This result uses the forest structure for unequal endpoint sums and exact common-edge cardinality m−d at equal sums.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Mean frequencies alone cannot specify co-occurrence. The two-sequence setup does not directly give the one-word reflection classification or the count B(n−2m−g−2d+2) necessary for the exact variance; the inspected prior results do not imply that formula as stated.

evidence: At g=0, H=0 is avoidance of nonoverlapping reverse-complement factors of the specified length. The code papers use this known predicate. A later Resultary palindrome-radius record analyzes a literal equality reflection graph and parity-specific counts.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: An avoidance statement is the zero-count event, not second moments of the count. The literal-palindrome comparison shares the alternating-reflection mechanism but uses different constraints and counts; in particular it does not furnish the arbitrary stem and loop truncation formula here.

exact_database_or_table.reasoning: Neither the duplication output multiplicity nor literal palindrome moments give a tabulation of all i<j disjoint reverse-complement stems with arbitrary m and g. An unrelated web result does not count as evidence of absence.

originality.rationale: Supported distinction: exact covariance support and finite variance for disjoint reverse-complement factor pairs within one iid uniform word. The stem predicate, counting means, and covariance methods for random word matching are not credited as new in themselves. The older Fitch comparison is explicitly access-limited.
residual_risks: No full Fitch text was available after lawful attempts; older expectation and same-center joint-frequency coverage cannot be excluded. The indexed comparison is bounded to accessible evidence.

value.rationale: The reflection-center description gives an exact second-moment baseline for a natural random-word statistic. Position overlap alone could suggest widespread covariance; the proof identifies precisely why most such pairs are independent and gives a correction for the rest. The successive Fano ratio (q+1)/(q−1) remains above the independent-event limit even for long rare stems, so the correction is quantitatively relevant rather than a boundary-only effect.
residual_risks: The value is a uniform random-word baseline and does not establish prediction of actual molecular folding, uncertainty under nonuniform sequence models, or a distributional limit.
